title: Uninvestment Check
concept: A quick check to tell the difference between someone needing space (still invested) and someone who may be pulling away — so you know which repair to reach for. Describe what you can see, not what you think it means.
whenToUse: When warmth is missing even in ordinary moments, repairs feel like going through the motions, you’ve stopped planning ahead together, or contempt has replaced frustration. Check monthly, or weekly if you’re worried.
steps: Each of you marks, on your own, which of the 8 signs (listed under Practise) you’ve noticed, then share. Describe behaviour you’ve seen — don’t claim to know the other person’s intent.
If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. The same goes for fear or coercion at any count.
0 signs → nothing to fix. 1–2 signs → likely needs space and small repairs (Micro-Repair, Morning + Evening Rhythm).

3 or more signs → may be pulling away. Book a Full Recovery conversation within a week. For drift, no one “caused” it: you both name your part. (A specific breach of trust goes to Trust Recovery instead.)
Set a time window to check whether you’re both leaning back in.

phrases.text: I’m noticing some distance. Do you just need space, or is something bigger going on?
I want a Full Recovery conversation. Can we book it for when we’re both calm?
Contempt means we can’t just carry on as normal.

working: A marks three signs, B marks four: fewer messages, only logistics, repairs on autopilot. They book a Full Recovery conversation within a week, then keep up their morning and evening check-ins for 21 days, looking back once a week.
notWorking: Waiting for “them to miss me” while contempt keeps growing. Every week without a booked conversation runs down the clock.
activity: The 8 signs — each of you marks, on your own: (1) fewer non-logistical check-ins, (2) less curiosity about each other, (3) avoiding future plans, (4) doing more on your own in place of shared time (time apart is healthy), (5) mostly practical conversations, (6) going-through-the-motions affection, (7) repairs that feel routine, (8) contempt instead of frustration. If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Otherwise count them: 0 = nothing to fix; 1–2 = likely needs space and small repairs; 3 or more = may be pulling away — book a Full Recovery conversation within a week. Check monthly, or weekly if you’re worried.
warn: If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Fear or coercion at any count: stop; safety and outside support come first.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
